newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rebels accuse S.Lanka army of attacking civilians.
newsitem.headline: Rebels accuse S.Lanka army of attacking civilians.

text.p: Separatist guerrillas on Monday accused the Sri Lankan army of shelling Tamil villages in the north of the country, killing, wounding or displacing large numbers of civilians.

Government troops, whose push into the guerrillas' northern Wanni stronghold has been halted by stiff resistance from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), are now raining artillery on civilians, an LTTE statement said.
"Sri Lanka's army, stalled just north of Omanthai, is continuing to hammer distant Tamil towns with long-range artillery," said the statement, issued by the LTTE's international office in London.

It said a 22-year-old girl died in an artillery barrage while several of her neighbours were wounded. Heavy shelling had forced civilians to leave their homes and take shelter in the jungle, the statement said.
A military spokesman in Colombo denied the LTTE's charges, saying troops engaged only identified enemy targets.
The Defence Ministry said it was the LTTE that fired at troops, who are fortifying their gains in areas captured from the rebels after a major offensive launched last month.
"Terrorists continue to fire mortars at the troops and troops carry out retaliatory artillery and mortar attacks to neutralise enemy fire," a ministry statement said.
Military officials said troops were clearing mines and fortifying areas north of Omanthai and Nedunkeni, captured over the past two weeks.
Troops have not advanced for the past six days.
Journalists are not allowed into the battle areas and are unable to confirm government or rebel reports.

Two army divisions, consisting of about 20,000 troops, launched Operation Jaya Sikuru, or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.

Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte, who visited Nedunkeni, 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya, over the weekend told troops that the government's military action to weaken the LTTE would continue systematically, state radio said on Monday.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed since the war began in 1983. The rebels say the toll is higher.
